name: Grace of An'she and Mu'sha

angles.text: As a tauren, you learn that life calls you to honor An'she and Mu'sha as faithfully as the Earthmother. Their reverence lies at the heart of tauren spiritual identity and reminds young braves of their duty.
As a tauren druid, you look to the sun and moon's eternal dance as nature's primal balance, guiding your understanding of its cosmic rhythms.
As a tauren shaman, you speak with the spirits of earth, fire, water, and air, and pay equal homage to the celestial twins whose light sustains living energy.
As a member of the Horde, you see the sacred rites on Red Cloud Mesa and the nature-revering ways the nomadic tauren bring to their allies.

faq.answer: An'she and Mu'sha are the sun and moon in tauren belief, honored as the Earthmother's twin eyes. They shine from above, unlike the spirits dwelling in Azeroth's soil, air, fire, and water. An'she brings warmth and life, while Mu'sha offers guidance and solace through the night.

aliases: why revere the sun and moon
faq.answer: Tauren teachings hold that balance is essential to existence. An'she and Mu'sha give living creatures energy, vision, and hope. By offering incense at a high place, tauren show respect for both celestial lights, whose constant benevolence mortal life depends on.
faq.q: Why do the tauren make offerings to the sun and moon?

aliases: how to find the incense shrine
faq.answer: The shrine lies in the high hills southeast of Red Cloud Mesa, overlooking the plains and just south of the thorny quilboar territories. Its height gives a clear, unobstructed view of the open sky, where smoke can rise toward the heavens.
faq.q: Where is the shrine of An'she and Mu'sha located?

faq.answer: Smoldering incense carries a traveler's prayer and respect toward the sun and moon. Its fragrant smoke rises from the burning embers. Cast them into the shrine fire to complete the rite and bring the pilgrim a tranquil sense of spiritual fulfillment.
faq.q: What is the significance of the smoldering incense?

faq.answer: The incense must still smolder when it reaches the shrine fire, so the journey calls for vigilance, speed, and care. Finish before the embers burn to cold ash, and keep them from water, which would extinguish them and spoil the offering.
faq.q: Why must the incense be delivered quickly and kept dry?

aliases: are quilboar a threat to pilgrims
faq.answer: Quilboar tribes occupy defended thorn dens in the hills just north of the shrine. The shrine rests at a quiet overlook south of their grounds, but travelers must avoid the quilboar brambles, where an attack could delay or disrupt the journey.
faq.q: Do the quilboar threaten the pilgrimage to the shrine?

faq.answer: Tauren call the moon Mu'sha, the loving left eye of the Earthmother, gazing down on mortal life. Night elves revere the same luminous white moon as Elune, while tauren tradition binds Mu'sha to her solar twin, An'she.
faq.q: How does Mu'sha compare to other cultures' views of the moon?

sections.body: Tauren honor An'she and Mu'sha as the sun and moon, the Earthmother's twin eyes. Elemental spirits dwell in Azeroth's stones, winds, and waters, while the celestial twins watch from the heights of heaven. As they cross the sky, they mark day and night and bring warmth, guidance, and hope to living creatures. For tauren, honoring them is a spiritual duty. Balance calls for reverence toward the land beneath your feet and the light above.
sections.title: The Eyes of the Earthmother

sections.body: Carry smoldering incense into the southeastern hills overlooking Red Cloud Mesa, just south of the prickly quilboar grounds. Make the journey with speed and care. Keep the embers dry and reach the shrine before they burn to cold ash. At the elevated shrine, cast them into the sacred fire. Their fragrant smoke carries your respect skyward, toward the sun and moon.
sections.title: An Offering on the Heights

summary: On Red Cloud Mesa, An'she and Mu'sha receive honor as the Earthmother's eyes. You carry smoldering incense to a shrine in the southeastern hills, where its smoke rises toward the sun and moon that bring warmth, life, and direction to the plains.
attribution: In-game quest text: Grace of An'she and Mu'sha
